title: Does Fine-Tuning on a Shared Teacher Increase Downstream Homogeneity? A Mini Replication

original_idea.body:
# Does Fine-Tuning on a Shared Teacher Increase Downstream Homogeneity? A Mini Replication

**Problem:** Does light fine-tuning (LoRA) of two different small base models on the SAME teacher's outputs make them measurably more homogeneous to each other?

**Direction:** Take two small open base models. LoRA-fine-tune each on a small shared set of a single teacher's responses. Measure inter-model homogeneity before vs after.

**Why it matters:** Synthetic data from a few teachers floods pipelines; if it homogenizes the ecosystem, that's a root cause of systemic risk.

**Relevant context:** Jailbreak Transferability from Shared Representations (arXiv:2506.12913); Correlated Errors (arXiv:2506.07962).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible root-cause demonstration (shared synthetic data homogenizes) but the catastrophic link is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires LoRA fine-tuning two models and a controlled before/after measurement - solid ML fundamentals needed.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused before/after homogeneity on a single shared-teacher LoRA; clear endpoint.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open base models, single-GPU LoRA; root-cause angle external work can do.

low_compute.reasoning: LoRA fine-tuning of two models is heavier than inference-only; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Distillation-raises-similarity known; controlled shared-teacher convergence demo partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Synthetic-data homogenization plausibly shown; controlled two-student demo partly open.
